samples.question: The sheet is off-white. Exactly one mark on it is pure black: a single thin cable that runs continuously from its left end to its right end and has exactly one height at every horizontal position it covers. One small red ring is drawn centred on a point of that cable; the cable passes straight through the middle of the ring. The ring splits the cable into two parts: the left part runs from the cable's left end to the ring centre, and the right part runs from the ring centre to the cable's right end. The length of a part means the distance travelled along the cable itself, following all of its rises and falls from one end of the part to the other; it is not the horizontal distance between the part's ends, so a part that covers less width can still be the longer one when it climbs and falls more steeply. The two parts are never equally long: their cable lengths always differ by at least thirty pixels. The pale coloured polylines, the grey border and the short grey tick marks are decoration and carry no information. Which part of the cable is longer? Answer with one word: left or right.
